name: Globus Medical, Inc.
moat_justification: Clear #2 in spine, effectively neck-and-neck with Medtronic post-NuVasive, with the ExcelsiusGPS/Excelsius ecosystem creating implant pull-through and surgeon switching friction; but ROIC only just recovered to 10.5% in FY2025 after 2.8%/4.2% in the merger years, gross margin is still below pre-merger levels, and Medtronic/Stryker/Zimmer/J&J contest every placement — a moderate moat, not a wide one.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 10.1%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 3.86 vs 3-yr median 2.55 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (9.8%) vs bull-case tier B (15.7%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Quality #2 spine franchise, moat 5/10, post-merger earnings recovering fast (TTM OE $5.09/share) — but at $75.65 the weighted IRR is 12.9%, short of the 15% hurdle; it clears 15% only at or below the $61.85 weighted IV@15%.
moat_for: #2 spine franchise at Medtronic's scale post-NuVasive (neck-and-neck on spine revenue), broadest musculoskeletal portfolio in the industry
ExcelsiusGPS robotics + ExcelsiusHub/3D ecosystem: installed robots pull through proprietary implants, instruments and service — a placement today is a recurring implant stream
Surgeon relationships and competitive recruiting: U.S. Spine grew 7% in Q2 2026, its fifth consecutive quarter of above-market growth
Vertical in-house manufacturing enabling rapid product iteration and supply control; 60+ projects in development
Debt-free balance sheet ($629M cash + marketable securities at FY2025 end) funds placements, leasing models and tuck-ins like Nevro
moat_against: ROIC history does not support a wide moat: 10.5% (2022) collapsed to 2.8% (2023) and 4.2% (2024) on merger amortization/integration and only recovered to 10.5% in FY2025
Gross margin still rebuilding: 74.2% (2022) -> 58.9% (2024) -> 67.4% (FY2025); management targets only low-70s by end-2026 and mid-70s in 2027
Robotics is contested, not owned: Medtronic Mazor/Stealth, Zimmer ROSA, Stryker and J&J all place rival platforms; surgeon loyalty is personal and reps can be poached
Enabling Technologies revenue fell 25.8% in Q2 2026 and Nevro fell 14.3% — the two newest growth legs are currently shrinking
Hospital capital budgets and procedure pricing pressure cap implant pricing power; spine market itself grows only ~3%/yr
